hunks.context: ## Publish ordering — do not publish between the fix and the re-run

lines.content: `berlin52` and `eil76` in the current prelim set) → then publish. A republish alone is not enough and
is worse than not publishing, because it attaches the new optima to old measurements.
The solver half merged as **#575** (`fe89b6a9`) and the benchmark re-run follows it in the published
shards, so most of the body is delivered. One criterion is still unmet, and the code says so:
const byType = { ATT: attDistance, CEIL_2D: ceilDistance, GEO: geoDistance }
`EUC_2D` is still excluded from `tourLength`, and the comment above it — "TSPLIB rounds it with
`nint()` and teeline does not" — became stale when #575 made teeline round the same way. So the
regenerated docs still fill `berlin52` 7542 and `a280` 2579 from TSPLIB's published list rather than
from the shipped `.opt.tour`, which is the criterion's point.
That is the remaining work: add `EUC_2D` to `byType` with `nint` rounding, correct the stale
comment, regenerate, and confirm the derived costs agree with the published ones. Small, and it
- [ ] `EUC_2D` distances are `nint`-rounded in both `KDPoint::distance` and the comparison path

changes.title: fix(solvers): EUC_2D must use TSPLIB's nint rounding, as Att and Ceil2D already do

commit.message:
task(solvers): say exactly what is left on EUC_2D rounding

The task cannot be closed: most of it shipped in #575, but
scripts/gen-problem-pages.mjs still excludes EUC_2D from tourLength, and the
comment justifying the exclusion became stale when #575 made teeline round the
same way TSPLIB does. Records the three-line fix so the next reader does not have
to rediscover why the criterion is unticked.
